caseno: CRIMINAL PETITION FOR LEAVE TO APPEAL NO. 167 OF 2002.
lawyer:
For the Petitioner :
Mr. A. Razzaque Khan, Additional Attorney-General, instructed by Mr. Md. Ataur Rahman Khan, Advocate-on-Record 
For the Respondent: 
Mr. Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record

The State ------ Petitioner 
Versus

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin J: - This petition for leave to appeal by the State is against the order dated October 29, 2002 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10038 of 2002 staying further proceeding of G.R. Case No. 585 of 2002 (arising out of Savar P.S. Case No.43 dated 20.8.2002) of the Court of Magistrate, Class, Dhaka (Kha area) and enlarging the respondent herein on ad interim bail. 

 2. The aforesaid Miscellaneous Case has been registered upon an application filed under section 561A read with section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashing of the proceeding of G.R. Case No. 585 of 2002 (arising out of Savar P.S. Case No.43 dated 20.8.2002) of the Court of Magistrate, Class, Dhaka (Kha area) and with a prayer for bail. 

 3. Savar P. S. Case No.43 dated 20.8.2002 has been registered upon an information lodged be one Md. Kafiluddin, stating, inter alia, that on 17.6.2001 the then leader of the opposition along with her party leaders and members were going to Pirojpur to attend a meeting that while they reached at Jadurchar area in Hemayetpur within Savar Police Station they could not proceed due to a barricade placed by 100 to 150 listed terrorists of Awami League, Chatra League and Jubo League that they reised different kinds of slogans in order to create panic and thereupon police force who were escorting the then leader of the opposition requested her to return back to Dhaka considering risk of her life. Although in connection with said incident information was lodged with Savar Police Station but instead of registering Case under the Specific Provision of law the said Police Station recorded a General Diary. That after restoration of Rule of Law on the assumption of power of the present Government the case as regard the incident of 17.6.2001 is being filed. 

 4. On receipt of aforesaid First Imformation Report Savar Police registered the Case No. 43 dated 20.8.2002 under sections 147, 148, 149, 341 and 506 of the Penal Code. 

 5. The respondent was arrested on October 20, 2002 and was produced before the Court on October 21, 2002 and thereafter was again produced before the Court on October 24, 2002 and on that date he was shown arrested in Savar P.S. Case No. 43 dated 20.8.2002. 

 6. The respondent in support of the petition before the High Court Division filed under section 561A read with section 498 of the Code of Criminal procedure submitted that the allegations in the FIR lodged on August 20, 2002 whereupon, Savar P.S. Case No. 43 dated 20. 8. 2002 has been registered, are false and politically motivated and that the said case has been filed against the respondent only to harass him. It was also submitted that as the proceeding of G. R. Case No. 585 of 2002 arising out of Savar P.S. Case No. 43 dated 20.8.2002 being harassing one against the respondent and also an abuse of the process of the court the same is liable to be quashed. 

 7. The learned Additional—Attorney—General submits that the petition under section 561A read with section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable since proceeding seeking quashing of which said petition has been filed in law at its present stage not liable to be quashed. It has further been submitted that the respondent as regard bail matter ought to have approached the courts below and that having had not done so prayer for bail ought not to have been considered by the High Court Division. It has also been submitted that since that petition filed under section 561A read with section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not well conceived one the High Court Division was in serious error in staying the proceeding of the G.R. Case No.585 of 2002 and that also in granting ad-interim bail. As against the submissions of the learned Additional Attorney General, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondent submits that the proceeding being harassing one and that also an abuse of the process of Court the High Court Division was quite correct in staying the further proceeding of G.R. Case No.585 of 2002 of the Court of Magistrate, l' Class, Dhaka (Kha area) and granting ad-interim bail. 8. Since the leave petition has been filed against the interlocutory order as such at this stage we do not like to make any observing upon the merit of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.10038 of 2002 registered on an application filed by the respondent under section 561A read with section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We are not inclined to grant leave to appeal as against the order of the High Court Division dated October 29, 2002 made in the aforementioned Criminal Miscellaneous Case in view of the order we propose to pass. 

 10. The order of the High Court Division staying the proceeding of G.R. Case No.585 of 

 2002 (arising Out of Savar P.S. Case No. 43 dated 20.8.2002) of the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka (Kha area) is modified and the investigation in the Savar P.S. Case No. 43 dated 20.8.2002 would proceed.
